title: Quasi-coherent sections descend along affine inverse limits
statement: Let I be a directed set [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and let (X_i) be an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit X [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix an index i and a quasi-coherent module F_i on X_i [pqf-def-coherent], write F_j for its pullback to each later X_j and F for its pullback to X. Then the canonical map \varinjlim_{j\geq i} \Gamma(X_j,F_j) \to \Gamma(X,F) is bijective; in particular, a section of F_i whose pullback to X is zero becomes zero after pullback to some later stage.

proof.text: Replace the directed system by the cofinal tail $I_{\ge i}$. The projections $g_j:X_j\to X_i$ and $g:X\to X_i$ remain affine, and the limit construction applies to this tail by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition].

Apply [lem-sc-valuation-limit-affine-pushforward-colimit] with $S_0=X_i$ and $\mathcal F_0=\mathcal F_i$. Writing $\mathcal A_j=(g_j)_*\mathcal O_{X_j}$, $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_{j\ge i}\mathcal A_j$, $\mathcal M_j=\mathcal F_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X_i}}\mathcal A_j$ and $\mathcal M=\mathcal F_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X_i}}\mathcal A$, it identifies $g_*\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal M$ and $(g_j)_*\mathcal F_j$ with $\mathcal M_j$, and identifies $\mathcal M$ with the directed colimit of the $\mathcal M_j$ in the category of $\mathcal O_{X_i}$-modules.

proof.text: The scheme $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so its quasi-compact opens form a basis and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qs-scheme-cohomology-directed-colimit] with $q=0$ and $U=X_i$ to the directed system $(\mathcal M_j)_{j\ge i}$ with colimit $\mathcal M$ (Step 2); since $H^0(X_i,-)=\Gamma(X_i,-)$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_{j\ge i}\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal M_j)\to\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal M)$ is bijective (Limits 01Z0 uses Sheaves 009F with Topology 0069 here).

For every $j\ge i$, the identification of Step 2 gives $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal M_j)=\Gamma(X_i,(g_j)_*\mathcal F_j)=\Gamma(X_j,\mathcal F_j)$, and likewise $\Gamma(X_i,\mathcal M)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$. Substituting these identifications into Step 3 yields the canonical bijection $\varinjlim_{j\ge i}\Gamma(X_j,\mathcal F_j)\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$. The final assertion follows from the zero criterion for a directed colimit of modules [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise]: a section at stage $i$ whose image in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ is zero has zero image in the colimit, hence becomes zero in $\Gamma(X_j,\mathcal F_j)$ for some $j\ge i$.
